transformations: Sort by NLSC TOWNCODE; derive foreign-twn-TOWNCODE stable IDs
Compact JSON and round coordinates to 6 decimal places; retain every source vertex and polygon component
No additional geometric simplification, no coastline clipping, no inferred historical boundaries
Create modern name search aliases; leave every historical_name empty
Leave every owner/controller unknown; parent_id is a suggested spatial editing reference only

historical_research.finding: THCTS documents Dutch/Spanish-period historical maps and thematic information; no reusable openly licensed 1640 whole-island tribal polygon coverage was verified.
Dutch-period eastern Taiwan gold exploration route/settlement study is a useful historical reference, not a verified closed tribal boundary dataset.
Alternative gbOpen ADM2 represents 2017 OSM/Wambacher Townships, reports 369 units and CC BY-SA 2.0; not selected over the 368-unit government-origin source.

limitations: This is the complete 368-unit modern source, not a reconstruction of 1640 indigenous communities, territorial control, or administrative boundaries.
The mirror has existing minor overlaps and imperfectly matching neighboring edges; they are documented and retained, not presented as a topology-perfect historical survey.
Modern coastlines may include reclamation and differ from 1640. No coarse Taiwan polygon is used to discard coastal material.
Kinmen, Matsu, Penghu and source-associated remote island components remain available but have no inferred 1640 owner or historical parent.
Toucheng and Cijin each contain a mixed multipart geometry with remote islands; their parent_id stays empty for component-aware integration.
Source territorial association of remote islands is retained as modern reference metadata only; no inference of sovereignty or actual control is made.
All historical_name values are intentionally empty; modern Taiwanese place names do not become 1640 names.
